abstract: We prove that on every infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space \(H\), there exist three real-valued Lipschitz functions with no common point of Fr\'echet differentiability. This gives a negative answer to a longstanding question of Lindenstrauss, Preiss, and Ti\v{s}er. The proof is constructive and relies on elementary calculus and finite-dimensional linear algebra. Since every Lipschitz map from a Hilbert space into $\mathbb R^2$ has a point of Fr\'echet differentiability, the target dimension three is optimal.
hook: Three Lipschitz functions on a Hilbert space can share no point of differentiability.
summary: On any infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, the author builds three real-valued Lipschitz functions that have no common point where all are Fréchet differentiable. This answers a long-standing question of Lindenstrauss, Preiss, and Tišer. The construction uses elementary calculus and finite-dimensional linear algebra. Three is the smallest possible number, since any two such functions always share a differentiability point.
title: Three Lipschitz functions on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces with no common point of Fr\'echet differentiability
